rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي هلال
rows.claim: The Companions called this sūra al-Maqbara, the Graveyard Sūra.
rows.anchor: وكان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعد بن أبي هلال يسمونها المقبرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان والجلال السيوطي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says all exegetes regard the sūra as Meccan; al-Suyūṭī calls that the more common view.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان عند جميع المفسرين وقال الجلال السيوطي على الأشهر

rows.speaker: أبو بريدة
rows.claim: Abū Burayda reports that two Ansari clans, Banū Ḥāritha and Banū al-Ḥārith, boasted of living members, then their dead, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بريدة فيها قال نزلت في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī selects the Medinan view, citing the Ansari occasion and other evidence for a Medinan revelation.
rows.anchor: ويدل لكونها مدنية وهو المختار ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي بريدة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says they had treated the saying about Adam's two valleys of wealth, desire for a third, and a belly filled only by earth as Qur'an until this sūra came; God accepts the repentance of the repentant.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ابن كعب قال كنا نرى هذا من القرآن لو أن لابن آدم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports that they continued to doubt punishment in the grave until this sūra was revealed; al-Ālūsī adds that grave punishment is mentioned only in Medinan material.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه مازلنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت ألهاكم التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has eight verses by consensus.
rows.anchor: وآيها ثمان بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar transmits the Prophet's question whether anyone can recite a thousand verses daily and his suggestion to recite this sūra.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ألا يستطيع أحدكم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports that whoever recites a thousand verses meets God smiling; the Prophet recited this sūra and said it equals a thousand verses.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من قرأ

rows.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
rows.claim: Ibn al-Milq explains the thousand-verse merit as one-sixth of the Qur'an's aims: knowing God, the straight path, return to God, the obedient, deniers, and stages of the way; al-Ālūsī says the true reason is beyond this.
rows.anchor: وذكر ناصر الدين بن الميلق في سر ذلك أن القرآن ستة آلاف ومائتا آية وكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's connection to the preceding sūra is evident.
rows.anchor: والأمر والله تعالى أعلم وراء ذلك ومناسبتها لما قبلها ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahw originally means heedlessness, then came to mean anything distracting; convention narrows it to a pleasurable distraction, close to play. Here it makes people heedless.
rows.anchor: وأصل اللهو الغفلة ثم شاعر في كل شاغر وخصه العرف بالشاغل الذي يسر المرء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines lahw as what distracts one from what matters and concerns; al-Ālūsī applies the sense of heedlessness here.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب اللهو ما يشغلك عما يعني ويهم وقيل ليس بذاك المراد به هنا الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takāthur is competing and boasting over numbers, each group claiming to be more numerous.
rows.anchor: التباري في الكثرة والتباهي بها بأن يقول هؤلاء نحن أكثر وهؤلاء نحن أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They counted all the living, then went to the graves and mentioned those buried there, competing in the number of the dead; the endpoint is included in the process.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استوعبتم عدد الأحياء صرتم إلى المقابر وانتقلتم إلى ذكر من فيها فتكاثرتم بالأموات

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competed in numbers; after the first counted the living, the second counted the dead and won.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي ومقاتل أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا أيهم أكثر عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the earlier occasion, grave-visiting is literal; in the clan story it means reaching the point of mentioning the dead, by metonymy or metaphor, and is best treated as a representation.
rows.anchor: وزيارة المقابر على ما تقدم على ظاهرها وأما على هذا فقد عبر بها عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as sarcastic: they act like people visiting graves without a sound purpose.
rows.anchor: وفي «الكشاف » عبر بذلك عما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers that grave visits should prompt reflection on death, but the boasters perversely made them a cause of heedlessness.
rows.anchor: فجعلوها سببا للغفلة وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting distracts from religion, the most important concern; suppressing the object of distraction magnifies it and intensifies the blame, condemning anything that distracts.
rows.anchor: وحذف الملهى عنه للتعظيم المأخوذ من الإبهام بالحذف والمبالغة في الذم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan explain that wealth and children distract people until death, with grave-visiting standing for dying.
rows.anchor: وصدره قد أخرجه ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس وهو ابن أبي حاتم وابن أبي شيبة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī cites an anonymous poem and Jarīr to show that visiting the graves can mean dying; the wording also points to resurrection.
rows.anchor:
وقال جرير :
زار القبور أبو مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab heard the verse and concluded that the people would be raised for Judgment, since a visitor eventually leaves rather than remaining.
rows.anchor: يحكى أن أعرابيا سمع ذلك فقال بعث القوم للقيامة ورب الكعبة

rows.speaker: مر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says every visitor must return either to the Garden or the Fire; the verse also signals the short stay in graves.
rows.anchor: وعن مر بن عبد العزيز أنه قال لا بد لمن زاد أن يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense indicates certainty, may include those who died first, or treats the ancestors' deaths as the listeners' own.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق الوقوع أو لتغليب من مات أولا أو لجعل موت آبائهم بمنزلة موتهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says God addresses the sūra to unbelievers on Judgment Day, reproaching them for graves they had already visited; al-Ālūsī finds this astonishing.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم أن الله عز وجل يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة تعييرا للكفار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the verse as reproaching excessive grave visits made to boast of the dead and one's visits rather than remember the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذا تأنيب على الإكثار من زيارة القبور تكثرا بمن سلف ومباهاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says that reading is far from the verse, though he cites the report that grave visits should remind one of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الآية بمعزل عن ذلك نعم لا كلام في ذم زيارة القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He condemns visiting graves to boast of the deceased or the visit, especially ignorant shrine-goers who treat innovations and abuses as acts of worship.
rows.anchor: نعم لا كلام في ذم زيارة القبور للتفاخر بالمزور أو للتباهي بالزيارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة
rows.claim: These readers lengthen the initial hamza in alhākum as an interrogative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة آلهاكم بالمد على الاستفهام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وابن عباس والشعبي وأبو العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use two hamzas in a question; the interrogative is for affirmation.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī parses alladhī as a full appositive for kull; an unlabelled alternative makes it a partitive appositive.
rows.anchor: الذي جَمَعَ مَالاً } بدل من { كل } بدل كل

rows.speaker: الجاربردي
rows.claim: Al-Jarbardī permits alladhī to be an adjective because kull is definite, by analogy with al-Zamakhsharī's analysis of 50:21; al-Ālūsī objects to this.
rows.anchor: وقال الجاربردي يجوز أن يكون صفة له لأنه معرفة على ما ذكره الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be accusative or nominative as a form of censure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا أو مرفوعا على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite mālan magnifies and multiplies the wealth; reports about al-Akhnas say he had four or ten thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: وتنكير مالا للتفخيم والتكثير وقد كان عند القائلين إنها نزلت في الأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite form diminishes the wealth as insignificant and contemptible in God's sight.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتحقير والتقليل باعتبار أنه عند الله تعالى أقل وأحقر شيء

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa for an intensive sense, fitting its coordination with ʿaddadah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان جمع بشد الميم للتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He repeatedly counted his wealth because of his love and passion for it.
rows.anchor: أي عدة مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: One explanation says he divided the wealth into kinds, such as real estate, goods, and coins.
rows.anchor: وقيل جعله أصنافا وأنواعا كعقار ومتاع ونقود حكاه في التأويلات

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several scholars say he made the wealth a reserve for the calamities and hardships of time.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد أي جعله عدة ومدخرا لنوائب الدهر ومصائبه

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read ʿaddadahu lightly, without gemination.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والكلبي وعدده بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading it is a past verb meaning he counted it, with dissimilation contrary to the usual rule; the cited poetic line supports the unusual form.
rows.anchor: فهو فعل ماض فك إدغامه على خلاف القياس كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it is the noun for a count, coordinated with māl: he collected the wealth and carefully counted it; al-Kashf says this does not require an awkward construction.
rows.anchor: هو اسم بمعنى العدد المعروف معطوف على ماله أي جمع ماله وضبط عدده وأحصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further noun sense is followers and supporters; he collected wealth and a numerous supporting retinue.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى الاتباع والأنصار يقال فلان ذو عدد وعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladahu may be circumstantial or a new independent clause.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية أو استئنافية وأخلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhlada and khallada mean to leave someone lasting forever or for a very long time.
rows.anchor: لا يتناهى أو مكثا طويلا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses an illustrative metaphor: wealth lengthens his hopes, so he builds, plants, and digs as if his money kept him alive.
rows.anchor: والكلام من باب الاستعارة التمثيلية والمرادان المال طول أمله ومناه الأماني البعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming māl explicitly rather than using a pronoun reinforces the point, while the past tense intensifies the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: والإظهار في مقام الإضمار لزيادة التقرير والتعبير بالماضي للمبالغة في المعنى المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may literally believe wealth grants immortality through arrogance and distraction from the Hereafter, or because he thinks life and health depend on visible causes and wealth.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد أنه حاسب ذلك حقيقة لفرط غروره واشتغاله بالجمع والتكاثر عما أمامه من قوارع الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A remote interpretation says the verse alludes to an actually immortalizing pursuit: working for the Hereafter; al-Ālūsī regards this as very far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد انه يحسب المال من المخلدات ولا نظر فيه إلى أن الخلود دنيوي

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests the miser is the subject of akhlada and wealth its object, meaning he thinks he can preserve his wealth forever; al-Ālūsī dismisses the analysis.
rows.anchor: وزعم عصام الدين أنه يحتمل أن يكون فاعل أخلد الحاسب ومفعوله المال أن يظن أن يحفظ ماله أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's inimitability is certain; al-Ālūsī says the useful task is to explain its aspect briefly, not prove its existence.
rows.anchor: أعجاز القرآن مما لا مرية فيه ولا شبهة تعتريه وأرى الاستدلال هنا عليه مما لا يحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
rows.claim: Some Muʿtazilites locate inimitability in the Qur'an's unusual meter and style; al-Ālūsī says many verses match Arab poetic meters and Musaylima also produced that meter.
rows.anchor: فذهب بعض المعتزلة إلى أن وجه إعجازه اشتماله على النظم الغريب والوزن العجيب والأسلوب المخالف

rows.speaker: الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says the Qur'an's miracle is unsurpassed eloquence; al-Ālūsī objects that comparisons remain uncertain, Arabic speakers could produce parts, Companions differed, proof was requested, and eloquence alone would not verify prophethood.
rows.anchor: وذهب الجاحظ إلى أنه اشتماله على البلاغة التي تتقاصر عنها سائر ضروب البلاغات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes reports of the unseen the Qur'an's miracle; al-Ālūsī says isolated accuracy has no defined threshold, would make soothsayers and the Torah miraculous, and cannot explain passages without such reports.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اشتماله على الأخبار بالغيب ورد أما أولا فبأن الإصابة في المرة والمرتين ليست من الخوارق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view locates the miracle in the Qur'an's lack of contradiction despite its length.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو كونه مع طوله وامتداده غير متناقض ولا مختلف وأبطل بوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī challenges the claim that the Qur'an lacks contradiction, citing the statement that the Prophet was not taught poetry although all poetic meters occur in it.
rows.anchor: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that the count is ten complete may seem obvious, but it prevents a mistaken reading that only seven are meant on returning.
rows.anchor: لتوهم ولو على بعد أن المراد وتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that ʿUthmān acknowledged Qur'anic grammatical errors: it is implausible that the Companions collectively wrote, missed, and left such errors uncorrected; he calls the report weak, disrupted, and disconnected.
rows.anchor: فالحق إن ذلك لا يصح عن عثمان والخبر ضعيف مضطرب منقطع

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد الأعلى
rows.claim: A report says that after the codex was completed, ʿUthmān praised the work and noticed something to be corrected by their tongues; al-Ālūsī says this means they later corrected dialectal forms at review.
rows.anchor: أحسنتم وأجملتم أرى شيئا سنقيمه بألسنتنا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In a report al-Ālūsī calls sound on the conditions of the two Ṣaḥīḥs, ʿĀʾisha says scribes erred in writing the forms inn hādhāni, al-muqīmīn, and al-ṣābiʾūn.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال سألت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن لحن القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī explains ʿĀʾisha's claim as choosing a less suitable dialect among the seven readings when unifying the community, not writing an impermissible error into the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بأن معنى قولها أخطأوا أي في اختيار الأولى من الأحرف السبعة لجمع الناس عليه لا أن الذي كتبوه من ذلك خطأ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read al-muqīmīn al-ṣalāh and called it a scribe's grammatical error; al-Ālūsī says laḥn can mean language or reading, and notes another reading and the grammarians' analyses.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the no-contradiction account, the whole Qur'an is miraculous as a complete work, so sound sermons or poetry and the shortness of individual sūras do not disprove it.
rows.anchor: عدم التناقض والإختلاف مع الطول والإمتداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars also cite the Qur'an's awe, the reciter's growing love despite repetition, its lasting presence, and God's promise to preserve it as features of its excellence.
rows.anchor: مثل الروعة التي تلحق قلوب سامعيه وأنه لا يمله تاليه بل يزداد حبا له بالترديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī's own view is that the whole Qur'an, including its shortest sūra, is miraculous in its order, eloquence, unseen reports, rational accord, and subtle meaning; some aspects may be hidden while others suffice.
rows.anchor: والذي يخطر بقلب هذا الفقير أن القرآن بجملته وأبعاضه حتى أقصر سورة منه معجز بالنظر إلى نظمه وبلاغته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He closes with an unattributed line comparing successive manifestations to stars, each setting star giving way to others.
rows.anchor: نجوم سماء كلما أنقض كوكب بدا كوكب تأوى إليه كواكب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī read fakk with fatḥa, raqabatan in the accusative, and aw aṭʿama as a past verb.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ،   وأبو عمرو ،   والكسائي

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers use the noun fakk in the nominative, raqabatin in the genitive, and iṭʿāmun as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون { فك } برفع الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakk al-raqaba means freeing a slave; a person who frees a slave thereby makes that slave a ransom from the Fire.
rows.anchor: وأراد بفك الرقبة وإطلاقها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet's promise that freeing a believing slave secures each corresponding limb of the emancipator from the Fire, including the private parts.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال :  "  سمعت

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguishes freeing a slave oneself from helping pay for a manumission; he also urges gifts of milk, aid to oppressed kin, feeding and watering the needy, enjoining right, or at least speaking good.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال :  "  جاء أعرابي إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets freeing a neck as freeing oneself from sins through repentance; masghaba means famine or hunger, from saghiba for becoming hungry.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة قوله : { فك رقبة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These acts of closeness benefit only when joined with faith.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أن هذه القرب إنما ينفع مع الإيمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says thumma here means wa, and does not mark sequence.
rows.anchor: وقيل :  " ثم "  بمعنى الواو ،   { وتواصوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawāṣaw means that they urge one another: patience in God's obligations and commands, and compassion toward people.
rows.anchor: { وتواصوا } أوصى بعضهم بعضاً ،   { بالصبر } على فرائض الله وأوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfala sāfilīn means old age and the most decrepit lifespan, when intellect declines and the body weakens; the elderly are lower in condition than the weak, chronically ill, and children.
rows.anchor: يريد إلى الهرم وأرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite asfala sāfilīn generalizes the category, as in the expression fulān akram qāʾim.
rows.anchor: فالشيخ الكبير أسفل من هؤلاء جميعاً

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh reads asfal al-sāfilīn with the definite article.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله أسفل السافلين

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Mujāhid interpret the phrase as returning people to the Fire, whose parts lie at different depths.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ،   وقتادة ،   ومجاهد : يعني ثم رددناه إلى النار

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says they are returned to the Fire in its worst form, as pigs.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية : يعني إلى النار في شر صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Fire interpretation of the previous verse, believers are excepted and are not returned to the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لا يردون إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the old-age interpretation, minds and deeds cease; believers continue receiving credit after senility for the righteous deeds they used to do when young and healthy.
rows.anchor: فإنه يكتب لهم بعد الهرم والخرف ،   مثل الذين كانوا يعملون في حال الشباب والصحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says some people in the Prophet's time reached the most decrepit age, and revelation excused them by preserving the reward earned before their minds failed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says old age did not harm the man because God ended his life upon the best deeds he had performed.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة : لم يضر هذا الشيخ كبره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through ʿIkrima attributes to Ibn ʿAbbās the view that the exception means those who read the Qur'an, who are not returned to decrepit age.
rows.anchor: عاصم الأحول عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means uncut off: the person's reward is recorded as the good they used to do.
rows.anchor: فلهم أجر غير ممنون } غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the reward comes without further deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : أجر بغير عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one whose scales are heavy is the one whose good deeds outweigh the other deeds.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فأما من ثقلت موازينه } رجحت حسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is in a pleasing, approved life in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فهو في عيشة راضية } مرضية في الجنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as a life possessing satisfaction, one its owner is pleased with.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one whose scales are light is the one whose evil deeds outweigh the good.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأما من خفت موازينه } رجحت سيئاته على حسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His dwelling is the Fire; it is called a mother because people naturally settle with their mothers. Al-Hāwiya is a name for Hell and a bottomless pit.
rows.anchor: الهاوية اسم من أسماء جهنم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says hāwiya is an Arabic expression used of someone who has fallen into a grave difficulty: hawat ummuhu.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : وهي كلمة عربية

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ummuhu as the top of his head: they fall into the Fire headfirst.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا التأويل ذهب قتادة وأبو صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Takāthur is Meccan and has eight verses.
rows.anchor: مكية ،   وآياتها ثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting and competing over wealth and numbers distract people from obeying their Lord and from what saves them from His anger.
rows.anchor: بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visiting the graves means that you died and were buried.
rows.anchor: حتى متم ودفنتم في المقابر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the sūra was revealed about Jews who boasted that their clans outnumbered others, remaining distracted until they died astray.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : نزلت في اليهود

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm competed over nobles and numbers; after ʿAbd Manāf first counted more living people, Sahm counted the dead and won by three households.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي : نزلت في حيين من قريش

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
rows.claim: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports from his father that the Prophet explained a person's wealth is only what he consumes, wears out, or gives away and sends ahead.
rows.anchor: عن مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير ،   عن أبيه

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that three follow the dead, but family and wealth return while deeds remain.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك يقول :  "  قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحفص وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa for an intensive sense; the remaining readers read it lightly.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ،   وابن عامر ،   وحفص ،   وحمزة ،   والكسائي : { جمع } بتشديد الميم على التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAddadahu means he counted and kept account of the wealth.
rows.anchor: أحصاه ،   وقال مقاتل : استعده وادخره

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says he prepared, stored, and made it a provision for himself; Arabic uses aʿdadtu and ʿadadtuhu for keeping something back.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : استعده وادخره وجعله عتاداً له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this world, imagining that his riches mean he will not die.
rows.anchor: يظن أنه لا يموت مع يساره
